source_refs.note: Topic 1.8.2, printed page 15: the reactions with oxygen. The print's 'MgO(g)' is given as the solid.

blocks.text: Sodium burns in oxygen with a golden yellow flame to produce a white solid mixture of sodium oxide and sodium peroxide. Sodium is kept under kerosene oil to prevent its reaction with air; in open air it reacts vigorously with oxygen to form the peroxide, 2Na(s) + O2(g) gives 2Na2O2(s). Under special conditions, such as limited oxygen or high temperature, sodium oxide is formed: 4Na(s) + O2(g) gives 2Na2O(s).
Magnesium burns in oxygen with an intense white flame to give white solid magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O2(g) gives 2MgO(s).

blocks.title: Magnesium flares
blocks.text: Magnesium powder burns very rapidly with an intense white flame, which has led to its use in fireworks and S.O.S. flares.

blocks.prompt: Why is sodium stored under kerosene oil, and what two products can it give with oxygen?
blocks.explanation: Sodium reacts vigorously with the oxygen of the air, so kerosene keeps the air away. In plenty of oxygen it forms sodium peroxide; with limited oxygen or at high temperature it forms sodium oxide.

items: Sodium burns with a golden yellow flame to sodium peroxide (2Na + O2 gives 2Na2O2), or sodium oxide with limited oxygen (4Na + O2 gives 2Na2O); it is kept under kerosene.
Magnesium burns with an intense white flame to magnesium oxide (2Mg + O2 gives 2MgO); the flame is used in fireworks and flares.
